back: An infection that is transmitted through sexual contact.
HIV is the virus; AIDS is the late stage of untreated infection, when the immune system is very weak.

front: How does HIV damage the body?
back: It destroys a type of lymphocyte, so fewer antibodies are made and opportunistic infections such as TB develop.
Unprotected sex, infected blood (shared needles, unscreened blood) and from mother to baby.
Not by hugging, shaking hands, sharing cups or food, toilets, swimming pools, coughs or mosquito bites.
Antiretroviral therapy keeps HIV very low so the immune system recovers; it must be taken daily and is not a cure.
notes: When the virus is undetectable, HIV is not passed on through sex.

front: Ways to control the spread of STIs
back: Abstinence, faithfulness, condoms, testing, treatment (antibiotics, ART), contact tracing, PMTCT and screening blood.
Finding and informing the sexual partners of a person with an STI so they can be tested and treated.
Gonorrhoea, syphilis and chancroid: curable with antibiotics.
HIV, genital herpes and genital warts (HPV): cannot be cured, but can be controlled.
Gonorrhoea: burning urination and discharge. Syphilis: painless sore, later a rash on the palms and soles.
